Topics · Is there a God?

If God wants my belief, why doesn't He appear?

The text asks this too. A partial answer: overwhelming sight ends free trust. It does not explain all silence.

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ ۖ وَلَوْ أَنزَلْنَا مَلَكًا لَّقُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنظَرُونَ٨ وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَـٰهُ مَلَكًا لَّجَعَلْنَـٰهُ رَجُلًا وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّا يَلْبِسُونَ٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "Why was there not sent down to him an angel?"[294] But if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided;[295] then they would not be reprieved. And if We had made him [i.e., the messenger] an angel, We would have made him [appear as] a man, and We would have covered them with that in which they cover themselves [i.e., confusion and doubt].

Translator's notes

[294] In support of his prophethood (ﷺ). [295] They would have been destroyed immediately with no chance for repentance.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:8-9

This may be the most honest question, and it is old. People asked it to the man who brought this book: why has no angel been sent down? So you are not the first. If an angel came as an angel, the matter would be over, with no room left for anyone's choice. If it came in human form, the same doubt would return. Either a sight forces the matter, or it leaves room to doubt. Is there a third kind? That is the strongest objection, and it stays open.

A question for you

What would change if God appeared to everyone now?

If you sayEveryone would believe, and that would be good.
ThenEveryone would know. The question is whether knowing like that is trust, which comes next.
If you sayEveryone would obey out of fear.
ThenThat is the argument's point: fear, not choice.
If you sayI am not asking for a huge appearance, only for something.
ThenThat is the strongest form of the question. This argument alone does not answer it, and this Step says so.
If you sayAn old miracle would do, if I could trust the report.
ThenThe text does not build its case there, and a whole question looks at why.

Part 2 of 4

﴿هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ أَوْ يَأْتِىَ رَبُّكَ أَوْ يَأْتِىَ بَعْضُ ءَايَـٰتِ رَبِّكَ ۗ يَوْمَ يَأْتِى بَعْضُ ءَايَـٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَـٰنُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ ءَامَنَتْ مِن قَبْلُ أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِىٓ إِيمَـٰنِهَا خَيْرًا ۗ قُلِ ٱنتَظِرُوٓا۟ إِنَّا مُنتَظِرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in tyranny and enmity until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims." Now? And you had disobeyed [Him] before and were of the corrupters?

Quran · Yunus 10:90-91

Translation

Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may come again on the Egyptians, on their chariots, and on their horsemen.” Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it. Yahweh overthrew the Egyptians in the middle of the sea. The waters returned, and covered the chariots and the horsemen, even all Pharaoh’s army that went in after them into the sea. There remained not so much as one of them.

Original · Hebrew

וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה נְטֵ֥ה אֶת־יָדְךָ֖ עַל־הַיָּ֑ם וְיָשֻׁ֤בוּ הַמַּ֨יִם֙ עַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם עַל־רִכְבּ֖וֹ וְעַל־פָּרָשָֽׁיו׃ וַיֵּט֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה אֶת־יָד֜וֹ עַל־הַיָּ֗ם וַיָּ֨שָׁב הַיָּ֜ם לִפְנ֥וֹת בֹּ֨קֶר֙ לְאֵ֣יתָנ֔וֹ וּמִצְרַ֖יִם נָסִ֣ים לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַיְנַעֵ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃ וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ הַמַּ֗יִם וַיְכַסּ֤וּ אֶת־הָרֶ֨כֶב֙ וְאֶת־הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים לְכֹל֙ חֵ֣יל פַּרְעֹ֔ה הַבָּאִ֥ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּיָּ֑ם לֹֽא־נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּהֶ֖ם עַד־אֶחָֽד׃

the Torah (Exodus) · 14:26-28

World English Bible

Why would overwhelming sight be a problem? Think of what is valuable in trust. If a person is sure of being watched by a judge in the room, their good behaviour tells you little about them. Faith may be similar: where the evidence is overwhelming, believing says little about the one who believes. The first text says that when a compelling sign comes, a new faith no longer counts. The second shows a man declaring belief as the water closes over him, when choice is gone.

A question for you

Would faith have value if the evidence were overwhelming?

If you sayNo. It becomes knowledge without trust.
ThenThen this hiddenness has some sense. How much hiddenness remains the question.
If you sayYes. I could know and still choose.
ThenThat is a strong reply. It weakens this answer, and the app does not hide that.
If you sayI don't care about its value. I want the truth.
ThenThat is serious. What follows is for you.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَ مُوسَىٰ لِمِيقَـٰتِنَا وَكَلَّمَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ قَالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِىٓ أَنظُرْ إِلَيْكَ ۚ قَالَ لَن تَرَىٰنِى وَلَـٰكِنِ ٱنظُرْ إِلَى ٱلْجَبَلِ فَإِنِ ٱسْتَقَرَّ مَكَانَهُۥ فَسَوْفَ تَرَىٰنِى ۚ فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُۥ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُۥ دَكًّا وَخَرَّ مُوسَىٰ صَعِقًا ۚ فَلَمَّآ أَفَاقَ قَالَ سُبْحَـٰنَكَ تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when Moses arrived at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You." [Allāh] said, "You will not see Me,[401] but look at the mountain; if it should remain in place, then you will see Me." But when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He rendered it level,[402] and Moses fell unconscious. And when he awoke, he said, "Exalted are You! I have repented to You, and I am the first [among my people] of the believers."[403]

Translator's notes

[401] That no one can see Allāh during the life of this world. [402] It crumbled to dust. [403] This is a severe warning from Allāh against rebellion.

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:143

Translation

Moses said, “Please show me your glory.” He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.” He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”

Original · Hebrew

וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַרְאֵ֥נִי נָ֖א אֶת־כְּבֹדֶֽךָ׃ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֲנִ֨י אַעֲבִ֤יר כָּל־טוּבִי֙ עַל־פָּנֶ֔יךָ וְקָרָ֧אתִֽי בְשֵׁ֛ם יְהוָ֖ה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְחַנֹּתִי֙ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָחֹ֔ן וְרִחַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲרַחֵֽם׃ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א תוּכַ֖ל לִרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־פָּנָ֑י כִּ֛י לֹֽא־יִרְאַ֥נִי הָאָדָ֖ם וָחָֽי׃

the Torah (Exodus) · 33:18-20

World English Bible

Wanting to see is human. Moses himself asks here: my Lord, show me, so I may look at You. He is told he will not see, and pointed at a mountain, which collapses. He falls, and on waking he turns back in repentance. The verse records no rebuke of his asking. Making sight the price of belief (2:55) is another matter. The honest limit: this explains why that vision is not given. It does not explain why those who sincerely seek may feel nothing at all.

A question for you

Which is closest to your experience?

If you sayI asked for a long time and nothing happened.
ThenThat is real. This app does not explain it by a fault in you.
If you sayI never asked, and I don't think anyone is there.
ThenThat is yours. The question stays with evidence, not asking.
If you sayI sometimes feel something, and don't trust it.
ThenThat caution is reasonable. It has its questions.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 145:18

World English Bible

One more thing is claimed, and it is the opposite of absence. This text says: I am near. It is not a proof, and you can't verify it from outside. But it changes the shape of the question. The picture is not of a distant ruler who won't come out. It is of someone closer than you think, who is not seen. Whether that is true, you will have to weigh. This page cannot weigh it for you.
